title: synchronize-emitter-tick-with-kv-prewarm-and-graded-credit-rebalancing
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context and motivation: Streaming generation at tail percentiles continues to be dominated by two interacting sources: (1) KV-cache cold starts that trigger async rehits and kernel rebinds, and (2) emission tick jitter caused by credit-window oscillation under mixed latency/throughput workloads. This PR implements a coordinated approach: a tight synchronous prewarm path for in-flight request prefixes, a micro-windowed emitter tick that aligns with prewarm completion, and a graded credit rebalancer that reduces per-emitter oscillation without sacrificing throughput.

Design summary: single continuous description covering goals, design, and testing. The implementation has three primary pieces: (A) kv_preload: a synchronous fast-path invoked at emission start when the prefix KV footprint is small or when the request is marked latency-sensitive; (B) emit_tick micro-window: the emitter loop now defers the first flush to a bounded micro-window (configurable default 400us) but will advance immediately if kv_preload signals ready; (C) graded_credit_rebalancer: replaces the binary credit bounce with a proportional-integral controller that gradually adjusts emitter credits across priority lanes to avoid abrupt flushes. The rebalancer uses observed per-emitter token completion rates and short-term variance to compute an adjustment factor.

Why this is different: rather than only tuning flush cadence or only prefetching, the PR couples prewarm completion signals with emission timing and introduces a smoothing controller for credits. That coupling lets us avoid unnecessary stalls waiting on large async prewarms while preventing credit thrash that previously amplified kernel scheduling latency spikes.

Compatibility and safety: the synchronous prewarm path is gated by a runtime config flag and by request metadata (latency_sensitive=true). Default behavior for existing customers is unchanged. The graded controller falls back to the previous binary behavior if the controller fails health checks. No public API changes.

Files changed (high level): src/runtime/kv_prefetch.rs - new module implementing synchronous and async prewarm paths and a small fast-path cache; src/runtime/emitter.rs - refactor emitter loop to add micro-window and prewarm handshake; src/scheduler/credit_rebalancer.rs - new controller implementation and metrics hooks; src/runtime/tests/streaming_latency.rs - new integration tests that simulate mixed traffic with latency-sensitive flags; docs/streaming-tuning.md - added operational notes and recommended knob values; ci/workflows/benchmarks.yml - update to capture 99/995 pctl TTFB.

Commits (summary): 1) introduce kv_preload fast-path and interface to emitter; 2) implement micro-windowed emitter tick and handshake with kv_preload; 3) add graded credit rebalancer and metric exports; 4) tests and bench harness; 5) config and docs; 6) fix flake in prewarm healthcheck and add fallback.

Runtime behavior and numbers: On our internal canary benches (gRPC streaming model, seq_len distribution matching chat workloads) we observed median TTFB change ~0% (unchanged), p95 improved ~6-9%, p99 improved ~12-18% across mixes with 10-30% latency-sensitive traffic. End-to-end token cost unchanged within noise. Observed reduction in emitter loop wakeups ~22% which reduced kernel scheduling churn in busy boxes.

Testing and QA: unit tests for controller math and prewarm health checks added. Integration tests simulate a mix of heavy long-context background batches and low-latency requests. Bench runs were repeated across three instance types (A100, H100, L4) with consistent p99 improvements. Stress test: 24 hour soak with bursty synthetic traffic; recovered to steady state without deadlocks.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag 'emit_kv_sync_v1' and 'credit_rebalancer_v2'. Gradual rollout: 0% -> 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with metrics alerting on prewarm-fallback-rate and token-shed events. If controller oscillates above threshold, automatic revert to binary credit mode is available.

Related work and references: this builds on prior work in streaming flush cadence and prefetching but intentionally separates concerns: rather than increasing microbatch size we reduce jitter by synchronizing signals. See internal Linear items and the benchmark notes in docs/streaming-tuning.md.

Migration notes: operators can tune micro-window (default 400us) and controller gain knobs (proportional/integral) via Redwood Console or runtime config. Default knobs are conservative.

Merge notes: squash-merged after reviewer approvals and two successful benchmark runs.

review_comments: Anjali Rao: Can we make the micro-window configurable per-tenant? I worry about multi-tenant variance.
Maya Chen: Yes, exposed via config and Console; defaults conservative. Added docs and tests to validate per-tenant override behavior.
Ben Park: The PI controller gains look plausible but add a safeguard to return to binary mode if variance spikes.
Maya Chen: Added controller healthchecks and automatic fallback with metric export.
Diego Martinez: Bench runs show reduced kernel churn on H100. Approving after flake fix.
CI bot: integration-bench run #2 shows p99 -14% on average for latency-sensitive mix.
Release captain: please include streaming-tuning.md in release notes with default knobs.
release_notes: Introduce synchronized kv prewarm fast-path and graded credit rebalancer to reduce streaming TTFB jitter. Default is gated; operators can enable via runtime flags. Observed p99 improvements of 12-18% in latency-sensitive mixes. No API changes.
